messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: mdivide_left, etc.
parts:
These are breaking the build on g++ version 4.2 that
ships with Mac:

i686-apple-darwin11-llvm-g++-4.2 (GCC) 4.2.1 (Based on Apple Inc.
build 5658) (LLVM build 2336.9.00)

The error is:

src/stan/prob/distributions/multivariate/continuous/inv_wishart.hpp:93:
error: no matching function for call to
ï¿½mdivide_left_tri(Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, -0x00000000000000001,
-0x00000000000000001, 0, -0x00000000000000001, -0x00000000000000001>&,
Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var, -0x00000000000000001,
-0x00000000000000001, 0, -0x00000000000000001, -0x00000000000000001>&)ï¿½

Those -1 mean this is essentially

mdivide_left_tri(matrix_d,matrix_d);

It's the case where Marcus generalized to conforming
matrices as well as just vectors. So that'd be:

mdivide_left_tri(matrix_v,vector_v);

in

stan/src/stan/agrad/matrix.cpp

We also are going to have problems if we don't do the same
with:

stan/src/stan/math/matrix.cpp

I don't know how clang++ is managing to compile these.

- Bob

parts:
This wasn't a problem with how mdivide_left and
siblings were declared/defined -- it's a problem with how
they were refactored into .cpp files for libstan.a.

We need to add all the signatures we actually plan
to use there (and in the function declarations in
stanc).

Daniel's going to take care of it, so you (Marcus)
shouldn't have to worry about it.

We'll eventually push through the same kind of change
you made for speeding up dot products into actual matrix
multiplies and vector-matrix multiplies. No rush, though,
as it won't change any functionality.

- Bob
